comments.body:
GROUNDING (3 parallel research streams) before Q1 of the brainstorm for epic 6f2d.

(1) CURRENT ENGINE (codebase map). Thin LINEAR DAG executor via graphlib.TopologicalSorter, single
synchronous pass — NO branching, NO dynamic fan-out, NO loops, NO parallelism; a Burr-tripwire test
(tests/unit/workflow/test_executor_tripwire.py) actively prevents these from growing. DSL = YAML with
scripted steps (uses:) + agent steps (prompt: <reviewer_id>), ${{steps.x.outputs.y}} substitution,
JSON-Schema + linter. Prompt library = git-canonical prompts-as-files (.rebar/prompts/<id>.md +
packaged reviewers/*.md), front-matter + variant overlays; Langfuse is read-replica/trace ONLY, never
the prompt-text source. Render = Mermaid, ONE-WAY only (code comment: "no round-trip risk"). Eval seam
= Inspect AI ([eval] extra), NOT promptfoo (promptfoo only mentioned as interop in WS-G). Reviewers:
only review_ticket is reframed as a (one-step) workflow; verify_completion is bespoke Python;
review_code/scan_spec dispatch directly to runners. Burr is the DOCUMENTED escape hatch the a88f design
named for exactly the non-linear/fan-out/parallel/durable-pause triggers.

(2) INTENT RECONSTRUCTION (rebar store). CRITICAL: there is NO design/brainstorm session log for the
workflow engine and NO verbatim user quote for "bidirectional visual editing." The "core user
requirement" framing exists ONLY in (a) the deferral story WS-I (1f3e, "out: bidirectional visual canvas
editor (out of scope)", justified as "no round-trip risk") and (b) the remediation epic 6f2d's OWN
reconstruction. The original epic a88f was titled "git-native, AGENT-EDITABLE workflows" and framed
editing as TEXT editing with the graph EXPLICITLY read-only. So the premise "a core requirement was
silently deferred" is itself partly a reconstruction; no record of the user ever asking for a visual
EDITOR (vs a viewer), and no record of user sign-off on the deferral.

(3) VISUAL-EDITING ECOSYSTEM SURVEY (web/prior-art). No off-the-shelf tool satisfies all rebar
constraints at once (git-native schema-validated TEXT as source of truth + true bidirectional authoring
+ embeddable/no-DB-ownership + scripted+agentic steps + dynamic fan-out + low adoption cost). Three
camps: DB/canvas-owns-the-workflow (n8n, Langflow, Flowise, Dify, Node-RED — bidirectional but the DB
or a diff-noisy JSON is the master, NOT your git text); code-owns-graph/UI-only-views (LangGraph Studio,
Temporal, Prefect, Dagster, Argo — observability, not authoring); canvas-primitives/build-your-own
(React Flow/@xyflow, Svelte/Vue Flow, Rete, JointJS — the explicit non-goal). Only BPMN/bpmn-js is a
mature off-the-shelf BIDIRECTIONAL editor whose fan-out semantics (multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics)
fit — but its XML co-mingles layout x/y (257-line diff for a 1-attr rename), needs a JS front-end, and
carries a permanent bpmn.io watermark. Net: the polished bidirectional editors achieve bidirectionality
PRECISELY by owning the workflow in a DB / diff-noisy format — adopting any of them means abandoning the
git-native-text invariant. The only constraint-preserving paths are (a) keep YAML canonical + build a
thin text<->diagram round-trip ourselves (which IS "building a canvas", the anti-pattern), or (b) BPMN
as an interchange/editing format with real diff+frontend costs.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
DEEP-RESEARCH RESULT (wf_3b8affe5-14b; 108 agents, 24/25 claims confirmed) — convergent with the
first-turn survey. Applied the new "interrogate novelty" lens.

VERDICT: nothing off-the-shelf satisfies all three of {git-native TEXT as single source of truth +
bidirectional visual editor + mixes LLM and deterministic steps}. Recommendation: KEEP the homegrown
YAML + thin-executor engine; the visual layer is a SEPARABLE, deferrable concern.

EVIDENCE (confirmed):
- Langflow (147K+ stars): DB-canonical (SQLite default); JSON is export/interchange, NOT source of
  truth; co-mingles layout (node x/y + viewport zoom) with semantics -> noisy diffs. Mixed LLM+code
  (Python per component). Adopting it breaks the git-text invariant.
- n8n: the cautionary FAILURE MODE — JSON co-mingles layout/IDs/timestamps; git pull does NOT 3-way
  merge ("Pull and override" loses local edits); vendor visual-diff UI exists to paper over noisy JSON;
  fair-code (Sustainable Use License), not OSI-open.
- CWL: TRUE text-canonical YAML/JSON, dynamic fan-out via scatter/gather — proves text-canonical + map
  is viable — BUT read-only viewer only (view.commonwl.org) and NO agentic/LLM-step concept.
- GitHub-Actions visual editors are the cleanest existence proof of "text-as-source + visual
  projection": JetBrains plugin keeps layout in a SIDECAR (.idea/githubActionsLayout.xml), YAML stays
  clean; timoa/workflow-editor serializes back to the authoritative YAML. BUT GHA-only, no LLM steps,
  immature (~11 stars), and timoa's round-trip is structural-not-byte-lossless (drops comments/
  whitespace -> first-save diff noise). [A "real-time bidirectional sync" sub-claim was REFUTED 0-3.]
- n8n-as-code (~1.4k stars): third-party inversion to .workflow.ts "easier for people and AGENTS to
  edit", repo (not DB) is source of truth, git-like push/pull w/ 3-way conflict resolution — proves
  agent-editability + source-of-truth inversion are achievable; still co-mingles layout.
- 2026 emerging (surfaced, lightly verified): Microsoft Conductor (deterministic orchestration for
  multi-agent AI workflows, May 2026), arXiv 2510.04173, "Open Agent Spec 2026" (blog).

NOVELTY ANALYSIS (per the new skill principle): our architecture is NOT novel as architecture — CWL +
the GHA editors validate "git-text source-of-truth + thin executor + visual-as-projection" for
deterministic workflows. It is novel ONLY in the combination {mixed LLM+deterministic + a bidirectional
editor}. WHY is that gap there? BENIGN reason: the popular AI-workflow tools (Langflow, n8n) are hosted
SaaS products for non-technical users — they need real-time multi-user collab, persistent runtime
state, and a polished canvas, which make a DATABASE the natural source of truth. Git-cleanliness and
agent-editing are simply not their constraints. So the absence is "the market optimizes for a different
user (humans in a SaaS) than rebar (agents in a git repo)", NOT "people tried git-text-canonical for AI
workflows and it failed." Green-flag novelty (a real gap from a different constraint set), with ONE real
remaining landmine: clean diffs require keeping layout OUT of the semantic text (sidecar OR
layout-free + deterministic auto-layout) AND comment/whitespace-preserving (byte-stable) serialization
if an editor ever round-trips.

CAVEATS (research-flagged gaps): THREAD 2 broad format survey (BPMN/Argo/Dify/Kestra/Flyte/Temporal/
Prefect/Dagster/Node-RED/2026 specs) largely UNVERIFIED in this pass (some covered by the first-turn
survey); THREAD 4 first-person "why DB-canonical" rationale is INFERRED, not directly sourced.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
ROUND 3 — corrections + relaxed-constraint research (3 subagents) for the 6f2d brainstorm.

LANGGRAPH CORRECTION (confirmed in code + docs): two layers, don't conflate. (a) AGENT-STEP runtime
IS a thin layer over an established lib: LangGraphRunner uses langchain.agents.create_agent + ToolStrategy
(runner.py:124-169), optional behind [agents]. Chosen for NATIVE Langfuse tracing (every other agent
framework needs OTel) — after a research spike + 2 Opus design reviews (docs/llm-framework.md). (b) The
WORKFLOW ORCHESTRATION spine is homegrown (stdlib graphlib topo-sort), deliberately NOT
LangGraph-as-engine / Temporal / Prefect / Burr. So Joe is right: LLM execution rides on LangChain/LangGraph;
only the thin DAG orchestrator is ours.

DESIGN-RATIONALE DIG: the "why" Joe remembered EXISTS, but there is NO dedicated a88f design *session log*
— the rationale lives in: docs/llm-framework.md (LangGraph-for-Langfuse + 2 Opus reviews), the a88f stories
(WS-C Burr tripwire; WS-I read-only-render deferral "no round-trip risk", no user sign-off; WS-F Langfuse
trace/replica-only; WS-K retire LangflowRunner stub), docs/architecture.md, and the 6f2d description. (A
subagent circularly cited THIS session's log ad3f as "the design log" — discount that.) KEY: the Burr
"tripwire" CI test names the 4 adoption triggers = {non-linear branching, dynamic fan-out, parallelism,
durable-pause}; executor state pre-shaped toward Burr's immutable State for a cheap migration.

CRITICAL CONNECTION: Joe's invariant I1 (human must edit LOOPS + CONDITIONAL GATES) trips the Burr
triggers (branching + loops). So the visual-edit requirement FORCES the executor to change regardless of
format — extend the homegrown executor, adopt Burr, or inherit a format-native engine.

VIABLE SHORTLIST under RELAXED constraints (diff-noise OK; heavy edit-deps OK; light runtime; LLM-editable):
1. BPMN — Camunda Modeler (MIT desktop, no watermark, v5.48 2026-06; edits local .bpmn = source of truth)
   or bpmn-js (watermark) + SpiffWorkflow (LGPL, pure-Python, one dep lxml, v3.1.2) OR a DIY xml.etree
   interpreter. Expresses XOR/OR/AND gateways, loops, multiInstance fan-out, scriptTask vs serviceTask,
   legal <rebar:*> extension elements. The ONLY family that needs NEITHER a new editor NOR a new engine.
   GOTCHAS: (a) LLMs are BAD at hand-editing raw BPMN XML — hallucinate IDs, verbose (BPMN Assistant
   arXiv 2509.24592: routing edits via a JSON IR cut failures 11->2, ~75% fewer tokens) => edit a compact
   IR, serialize to BPMN. (b) DI/layout co-mingled with semantics in ONE file -> a semantic node w/o a
   BPMNShape opens INVISIBLE, silently; bpmn-auto-layout is all-or-nothing (clobbers hand layout). (c)
   custom <rebar:*> elements need a REGISTERED moddle descriptor or they're stripped silently on save.
   (d) XSD validates ~54% of constraints, 0% of references -> need a bpmnlint-style semantic gate. (e)
   BPMN's enterprise heaviness clashes with rebar's lean GH-Actions aesthetic.
2. draw.io + custom shape library over rebar's OWN IR — drawio-desktop (Apache-2.0, offline, v30 2026-06),
   uncompressed XML, custom shapes + <object> metadata round-trip, official drawio-mcp for agent edits.
   Keep rebar's lean executor (EXTENDED for loops/branch/fan-out = the Burr moment). RISK: draw.io enforces
   NO schema -> rebar owns the whole drawio<->IR validator + mapping; possible two-artifact (YAML + .drawio)
   sync. Keeps agents on our friendly format; no JS/engine lock-in.
3. ASL (Amazon States Language) — mature JSON spec (Choice/Map/loops), off-the-shelf bidirectional editor =
   AWS Toolkit for VS Code Workflow Studio (Apache-2.0, offline on local .asl.json). Agent-friendlier than
   XML; schema-validatable (asl-validator/statelint). COSTS: build an ~8-state Python interpreter (no live
   OSS Python runtime); editor is VS-Code-bound; no native LLM step (Task-as-agent-step mapping).

REJECTED/traps (cited): XState/Stately (JS-locked, SaaS editor, dead xstate-python), SCXML (no good OSS
editor; python-statemachine has an SCXML reader but editors are Windows-only/IDE-bound/0-star), Node-RED
(JS-coupled, no Python exec, minified flows.json), litegraph.js (more glue, Canvas2D, quiet), react-flow/
rete/drawflow (build-your-own libraries = the non-goal), Langflow/n8n/Flowise/Dify/Kestra/Windmill
(DB-canonical, breaks file-source-of-truth), LangGraph Studio (code-canonical, read-only debugger),
promptflow (deprecated 2027, no loops), MS Conductor / Oracle WayFlow (file+Python but NO visual editor yet).

CORE TENSION (flag to Joe): the formats best for HUMAN visual editing (BPMN/draw.io XML) are the WORST for
LLM editing (I2); the agent-friendliest format (our YAML/JSON IR) has no off-the-shelf editor. => points
toward a DUAL-representation design (clean rebar IR as the agent+execution source of truth + a round-tripped
visual format for the editor), OR ASL-JSON as the single-format compromise. NOTE: novelty check — all three
shortlist options are PROVEN OSS patterns, not novel; BPMN is the most-trodden + standards-based.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
EXECUTOR SPIKE (control flow: conditionals/loops/fan-out) — Plan agent, read-only, file-cited.

WHERE THE ACYCLIC/ONCE ASSUMPTION LIVES: executor.static_order (graphlib.TopologicalSorter -> CycleError
on any back-edge; executor.py:364-370); the single forward pass `for step_id in static_order(doc)`
(:459, each step visited once); `if:` is a SKIP-guard not branching (_guard_passes :383-400 — never
changes which step runs next); lint forbids cycles + >1 terminal (_ancestors :141-155; lint_document
:380-399) and requires refs point to a transitive `needs` ANCESTOR (:190-200); schema
additionalProperties:false (any new control-flow key is a hard error until a version bump).

IDEMPOTENCY BREAKS UNDER LOOPS (the riskiest change, same for every option): markers are keyed
(run_id, step_id) with per-key LWW (_processors.py:417-423) -> looping a step (1) collides/erases prior
iterations, (2) the succeeded-marker idempotent-skip short-circuits the loop after iter 1 (:471-475), (3)
side-effect tokens collapse (comment_verdict [rebar-run run/step], steps.py:175). FIX: iteration-keyed
markers (run_id, step_id, iteration) + per-iteration nondeterminism capture + side-effect tokens carry the
iteration + a MANDATORY max_iterations bound (each iter is a committed, auto-pushed event -> an unbounded
loop is a remote-store DoS, not just a hang).

OPTIONS:
(a) EXTEND THE HOMEGROWN EXECUTOR with a synchronous deterministic worklist INTERPRETER over a v2 DSL that
    adds DECLARATIVE route:/loop:/map: constructs (control flow as DATA). Zero new deps; pure-scripted
    workflows stay stdlib-only; stays thin/deterministic/event-sourced; does NOT trip the tripwire (still
    no async/threading/retry — the ban is on concurrency, not control flow), but DELIBERATELY overrides the
    documented Burr trigger #2 (must be recorded). RECOMMENDED.
(b) ADOPT BURR (the documented escape hatch) — fallback ONLY if durable cross-process pause/resume or TRUE
    parallel step execution lands. Heavier dep on the lean core; more imperative DSL (less projectable);
    we STILL hand-write the event-sourced persister, so Burr doesn't solve the genuinely-hard part.
(c) LANGGRAPH AS THE ORCHESTRATOR — REJECT. Would make langgraph a RUNTIME dep for ALL workflows incl
    pure-scripted (breaks the CI-enforced lean-core invariant: today `import rebar.llm` is stdlib-only,
    langgraph is lazy-imported only for agent steps); a LangGraph StateGraph is built IMPERATIVELY in
    Python -> NOT losslessly projectable to a canvas and can't round-trip from a visual edit (defeats the
    persisted-IR direction); fights the event-sourced run model (LangGraph's own checkpointer). KEEP
    LangGraph exactly where it is = the per-agent-step runtime (runner.py).
(d) FORMAT-NATIVE ENGINE (SpiffWorkflow/BPMN) — out of scope unless we adopt BPMN as the source format
    wholesale (throws away the hardened YAML loader / expression allow-list / injection guards / migration).

KEY CONNECTION TO THE VISUAL DIRECTION: a DECLARATIVE control-flow IR (route/loop/map as YAML data) is the
ONLY option that cleanly PROJECTS to a canvas and ROUND-TRIPS — exactly Joe's "persist the LLM-friendly IR,
ephemeral visual editor" architecture. An imperative LangGraph/Burr graph lives in code, not data, and
cannot round-trip. So the executor decision and the visual-editor decision REINFORCE each other: extend our
own executor with a declarative control-flow IR; LangGraph stays the agent-step runtime only. (This gently
corrects the framing of "change our LangGraph implementation to add control flow" — the control flow
belongs in OUR IR/executor, not in LangGraph.)

CRITICAL FILES: executor.py, lint.py, reducer/_processors.py, schemas/workflow.v1.schema.json (+v2) &
workflow/migrate.py, tests/unit/workflow/test_executor_tripwire.py. Ordered change list captured in spike.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
CONVERSION/ROUND-TRIP RESEARCH (wf_c717e2e3-917; 104 agents, 25/25 confirmed). Closes the visual-layer loop.

HEADLINE: there is NO zero-bespoke off-the-shelf solution for {persisted custom IR + ephemeral
off-the-shelf visual editor + reliable round-trip}; SOME thin mapping is unavoidable. The smallest proven
path = a THIN, ID-preserving IR<->standard-format SERIALIZER feeding an off-the-shelf EMBEDDABLE editor
that reads that standard NATIVELY as a transient projection. The serializer is the ONLY bespoke piece.

LLM-EDIT SIDE (Thread A) — converged 2025-2026 pattern: route LLM edits through a concise, ordered,
schema-constrained JSON IR via ATOMIC, ID-KEYED operations (add/delete/move/update/redirect), NOT raw-XML
and NOT whole-document rewrite. Evidence: BPMN Assistant arXiv 2509.24592 (peer-pub MDPI App.Sci.):
JSON-IR+atomic-ops cut editing FAILURES 11->2, output tokens >75%, latency ~43% across GPT-5.1/Claude-4.5-
Sonnet/DeepSeek-V3. NUANCE: the XML penalty is concentrated in EDITING; de-novo GENERATION handles XML
fine. Grammar/structured-output decoding (llguidance — Python bindings; Outlines/Guidance/XGrammar) can
guarantee syntactic validity; for hosted Claude, rely on provider tool-use/JSON-schema.

VISUAL ROUND-TRIP SIDE (Threads B/C):
- AVOID the MDE frameworks (Eclipse GLSP / Sirius Web / Sprotty / Langium): all are frameworks-you-build-on
  (need a custom metamodel->graphical mapping = the bespoke layer we want to avoid) AND runtime-locked —
  GLSP/Sprotty/Langium JS/browser-locked, Sirius Web JVM-locked + needs PostgreSQL + persists the model in
  a DB (violates "nothing persisted"). Hostile to a Python engine.
- TWO viable off-the-shelf "import structured format -> edit visually -> export back -> editor owns NO file"
  editors: (1) bpmn-js (importXML/saveXML over standard BPMN 2.0 XML; XML stays externally owned; needs DI
  layout to render -> bpmn-auto-layout generates it deterministically). (2) draw.io/diagrams.net EMBED mode
  (iframe + postMessage: init -> load{xml} -> save/autosave{xml}; HOST owns storage; Apache-2.0; drawio-mcp
  exists). BOTH are JS/browser -> run as an OUT-OF-PROCESS edit-time tool (fine per I4).
- BECAUSE rebar won't persist the visual format: layout-in-git / clean-diff / merge-on-layout gotchas
  DISAPPEAR; what REMAINS = semantic round-trip fidelity, STABLE IDs across the round-trip, re-layout on
  every open (mitigated by deterministic auto-layout; or a git-ignored ephemeral layout sidecar).

RANKED CONCLUSION: (1) if semantics are BPMN-shaped -> IR<->BPMN 2.0 XML + bpmn-js; (2) general diagrams ->
IR<->draw.io mxGraphModel + draw.io embed; (3) AVOID MDE frameworks. Open Q (empirical, spike-worthy): does
rebar's IR map cleanly to BPMN (agent/LLM step has NO native BPMN concept -> serviceTask+extension; fan-out
-> multi-instance), or is draw.io's free-form mxGraphModel + a semantic-tagging convention the safer general
choice? Do the editors preserve UNKNOWN/extension attributes so agent-step metadata survives a round-trip?
Is auto-layout deterministic enough, or persist an ephemeral git-ignored layout sidecar?

=== CONVERGED ARCHITECTURE (synthesis of 4 research rounds + 2 spikes) ===
1. SOURCE OF TRUTH (git): rebar's own LLM-friendly DECLARATIVE workflow IR (v1 YAML -> v2) extended with
   DECLARATIVE control-flow as DATA (route/conditional-edges, loop frames, map/fan-out) + STABLE element IDs.
2. EXECUTION: extend the homegrown thin executor into a synchronous deterministic worklist INTERPRETER over
   the declarative IR (spike option a). LangGraph stays the per-agent-step runtime ONLY. Iteration-keyed
   run-state markers + mandatory max_iterations.
3. LLM EDITING (I2): agents edit the IR via ATOMIC ID-keyed ops (MCP/CLI/file) + validate-then-repair vs
   schema+linter (BPMN-Assistant pattern applied to OUR IR). Optional structured-output/grammar constraint.
4. HUMAN VISUAL EDIT (I1), EPHEMERAL: a THIN IR<->standard serializer projects the IR to a standard an
   off-the-shelf embeddable editor reads natively (bpmn-js+BPMN, or draw.io+mxGraphModel), edited in a
   transient view, round-tripped back; visual format NEVER committed. Editor = out-of-process edit-time tool.
5. ONLY BESPOKE PIECE: the thin ID/ordering/metadata-preserving IR<->standard serializer. Everything else
   off-the-shelf. NOVELTY CHECK: every component is a proven pattern (CWL/GHA/ASL declarative IR; thin
   interpreter; BPMN-Assistant atomic-ops; bpmn-js/draw.io ephemeral-projection) — no novel-no-prior-art part.

LAST MAJOR OPEN FORK: which editor/format for the ephemeral visual layer — bpmn-js+BPMN vs draw.io+
mxGraphModel — likely resolved by a small serializer+round-trip SPIKE on a real rebar workflow.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
ROUND 5 — 3 spikes (codebase + 2 web) on agent runtime + engine/format. Convergent. Reshapes architecture.

SPIKE A (codebase: agent vs non-agent turns):
- PRODUCTION rebar.llm has NO single-turn/no-tools path. EVERY LLM turn goes through LangGraph create_agent.
  Even "extract" mode builds an agent-with-tools then does a SEPARATE with_structured_output().invoke()
  extraction call (runner.py:152,318). So a single-turn criterion runs as a zero/low-tool AGENT — overkill.
- LangGraph SURFACE actually used: create_agent (ReAct loop) + ToolStrategy (forced tool_choice for
  structured output) + init_chat_model (provider-agnostic). NONE of LangGraph's graph/state/checkpoint
  machinery is used. rebar pays for the whole runtime to use the prebuilt loop.
- Dep weight: [agents] = langchain>=1, langgraph==1.2.5 (PINNED, version-fragile), langgraph-prebuilt,
  langgraph-checkpoint, langchain-anthropic, langchain-openai, langchain-mcp-adapters, langfuse, pydantic,
  deepagents -> ~80-110 transitive deps. Tracing = Langfuse via LangChain CallbackHandler (tightly coupled).
- Runner seam (Runner Protocol: run/preflight; Fake/LangGraph/DeepAgents) is clean conceptually, BUT tool +
  structured-output contracts are LangChain-specific -> a new runtime needs BRIDGING code, not a pure drop-in.

SPIKE B (agent runtime alternatives):
- The LangGraph rationale is DEAD: "native Langfuse tracing" is no longer unique in 2026 — Langfuse is
  OTel-native (OTLP ingestion) and the LangChain CallbackHandler is itself OTel-backed; Pydantic AI / OpenAI
  Agents SDK / smolagents / Claude Agent SDK all have first-class Langfuse integrations via OTel.
- Anthropic now has GA grammar-constrained structured output (output_format) + native MCP connector ->
  removes the ToolStrategy machinery rebar fights (forced tool_choice breaks extended-thinking).
- RECOMMEND: PYDANTIC AI (pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,mcp]) — one framework covers BOTH single-turn typed
  calls AND tool-using agents; native MCP, decorator tools, first-class output_type, provider-agnostic w/
  Claude native, native OTel->Langfuse; much lighter; DELETES the ToolStrategy workaround + dual extraction
  path + fragile pinned trio. Runner-up: raw anthropic SDK + MCP SDK (lightest; ~100-200 LOC hand loop; own
  OTel; loses agnosticism). REJECT Claude Agent SDK (Claude-locked -> fails agnosticism; ~12s subprocess
  cold-start kills single-turn; 0.x alpha). Doc drift noted: docs/llm-framework.md claims prompts come from
  Langfuse get_prompt but prompts.py is git-canonical only.

SPIKE C (engine + format): FORMAT and ENGINE are INDEPENDENT axes.
- FORMAT: tailored LEAN declarative YAML/JSON IR (steps + if + loop + map), NOT a heavyweight standard
  (BPMN/ASL). Relaxed diff-noise does NOT rescue standards — their cost is the enterprise data model +
  agent-step impedance, not diffs.
- ENGINE: BUILD a thin synchronous interpreter (~300-600 LOC). Every off-the-shelf engine OWNS its run-state
  lifecycle, which CONFLICTS with rebar's event-sourcing (rebar IS the durability layer). Off-the-shelf field
  collapses: code-defined engines (Prefect/Dagster/Temporal/Airflow/Hatchet/Burr) fail the
  declarative-data/visual axes (Burr in-process but code-defined); Windmill is declarative+visual but
  server+Postgres+AGPL; ASL/DMN/CMMN/Serverless-Workflow have no maintained pure-Python in-process runtime;
  SCXML (python-statemachine) viable but no native dynamic fan-out; CWL steps are CLI tools (no in-process
  LLM). SpiffWorkflow+BPMN is the one serious contender (pure-Python, lxml-only, gateways/loops/multi-instance,
  best visual-editor story) BUT owns its run-state (serialize-whole-workflow blob) -> direct impedance with
  event-sourcing; heavy BPMN data model; no native agentic step; LGPL.
- NUANCE for Joe's novelty-skepticism: the thin interpreter is "good custom code" not "reinventing the wheel"
  — the off-the-shelf wheels don't fit the event-sourced AXLE. The reason to build is SPECIFIC and earned
  (rebar must own run-state); if that constraint were dropped, SpiffWorkflow is the only reconsideration.

CONVERGED STACK (provisional, to pressure-test): (1) agent runtime = Pydantic AI behind the existing Runner
seam (swap LangGraph); (2) engine = thin declarative interpreter over a tailored lean IR, run-state on the
event log; (3) visual = thin IR<->standard serializer + off-the-shelf embeddable editor (bpmn-js/draw.io),
ephemeral. Custom code confined to: the Runner adapter, the interpreter core, the IR<->editor serializer —
all "interface to rebar", except the interpreter which is justified by event-sourced run-state ownership.

VERDICT: evidence SUPPORTS the converged stack, with ONE sharp caveat (agent-runtime structured-output path).

ENGINE (build thin interpreter) — VALIDATED + Joe's skepticism resolved with evidence. The "durable
execution as a library" prior art validates the in-process SHAPE but UNIFORMLY refutes adopting any of them:
DBOS owns its store (Postgres/SQLite IS the source of truth; MIT, ~1.4k*, v2.24 2026-06); Restate is

[Refuted my provisional "DBOS does not own Postgres" — it DOES own it.]

Claude first-class, tools + MCP over 4 transports) reduces to ONE compact declarative YAML node
(io.kestra.plugin.ai.agent.AIAgent; only prompt+provider required; Apache-2.0, v1.12 2026-06). JVM/server-

draw.io embeddability + IR<->standard round-trip fidelity NOT verified => round-trip POC needed.

AGENT RUNTIME (Pydantic AI behind the Runner seam) — VALIDATED as seam-friendly (Pydantic AI's own DBOSAgent
wrapper proves the pluggable-runner-seam pattern is first-class). STRONGEST COUNTER-EVIDENCE (the #1 thing
to de-risk): Claude extended THINKING + forced-tool STRUCTURED OUTPUT is incompatible at the ANTHROPIC API
level (400: "Thinking may not be enabled when tool_choice forces tool use"); Pydantic AI's DEFAULT
structured mode (ToolOutput) forces tool_choice='any' -> hits it; AND anthropic-sdk-python #1204 (OPEN
Feb-Jun 2026, claude-sonnet-4-5/4-6): thinking+tools+json_schema structured output "broken or highly
unstable". CRUCIAL: this is API/SDK-level, NOT framework-specific — it ALSO affects rebar's CURRENT
LangGraph ToolStrategy path (codebase already documents that incompatibility). MITIGATION: use PromptedOutput
(not forced-tool ToolOutput), or Anthropic's GA grammar-constrained output_format (provider-native, no forced
tool_choice) — which STRENGTHENS the raw-anthropic-SDK+output_format option. SECONDARY: Pydantic AI churn
(~8-9 breaking 0.x releases Apr-Sep 2025; now 1.x stable BUT a 2.0 beta June 2026 = another wave) + a Jan-2026
maintainer-bandwidth crisis => ENFORCE the runner seam strictly so the dep stays swappable.
GOOD NEWS (refuted bad framings): "Langfuse-via-OTel from Pydantic AI is unsupported" REFUTED 0-3 (the
load-bearing premise for dropping LangChain survives); "Pydantic AI has no 2.0" refuted; "maintainer says AI
made them slower" refuted. OPEN: positively verify Pydantic-AI->Langfuse OTel TRACE FIDELITY to a non-Logfire
backend (load-bearing) => de-risk POC.

GROUNDING METHODOLOGY: promptfoo (exit-100 CI gating) complements rebar's existing Inspect AI evals; tau2-bench
as a tool-use benchmark reference. The 3 de-risk experiments (one per decision): (1) RUNTIME — golden-set eval

NET: keep the converged stack; (a) make the Runner seam non-negotiable (contains Pydantic AI churn), (b)

comments.body:
ROUND 7 — Joe's challenge batch: codebase verification + visual POC + web evidence.

RUN-STATE REUSE (Joe's "pattern matching vs reuse" challenge) — VERDICT: GENUINE REUSE, settled by code.
WORKFLOW_RUN/WORKFLOW_STEP are first-class event types (KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES _version.py:80-86; EVENT_TYPES
allow-list event_append.py). Emitted by TicketEventRecorder (executor.py:213-256) via _seam.append_event ->
event_append.write_and_push — the SAME locked write+push path as CREATE/EDIT/TRANSITION/COMMENT/TAG_DELTA.
Reduced by the SAME reducer (process_workflow_run/process_workflow_step, _processors.py:385-424, dispatched
:626-629 alongside all ticket events); compacted into SNAPSHOTs; per-key LWW + HLC-UUID order -> converges
across clones. Run-state is stored as events ON THE TARGET TICKET'S log; status/result READ via the same
reducer (show_ticket). So it is NOT a parallel store — the event-sourced SUBSTRATE (append/reduce/commit/
push/converge) is general-purpose; tickets are one schema on it, workflow run-state is another schema on the
SAME substrate, attached to the ticket the workflow operates on. Implications: a DURABLE run requires an
associated ticket (no ticket -> MemoryRecorder, ephemeral); run/step events kept OUT of hot paths via lazy
maps (setdefault), same discipline as session_log. Our new thin interpreter REUSES this recorder (extended
with iteration-keyed step markers per the engine POC) — extends existing reuse, not a new system.

DETERMINISTIC STEPS internal-only — CONFIRMED: STEP_REGISTRY (steps.py) is internal Python via @register_step;
NOT exported by the library, NOT in CLI, NOT an MCP tool. MCP exposes run_workflow (takes a YAML), never
individual steps. Matches Joe's requirement (deterministic logic internal, not client CLI/MCP surface).

LANGFUSE optional/client-light — CONFIRMED: in the [agents] extra (optional), lazy-imported inside _trace(),
no-op unless BOTH keys set (runner.py:527-550). Dev/observability only, not a client runtime dep. In the NEW
design it moves to a [tracing] OTel exporter (Langfuse = an OTLP endpoint) -> even lighter; clients who don't
set keys pay nothing.

OTel->LANGFUSE FIDELITY (Joe: find projects that confirmed it) — CONFIRMED SOLID: Langfuse has a dedicated
Pydantic AI integration guide + cookbook + OTLP endpoint (/api/public/otel); nested fidelity (agent run ->
LLM call -> tool span) confirmed by MAINTAINERS (pydantic-ai#3186 MCP-nesting fixed; #875 OTel-GenAI closed;
#3580 "everything working" vs Langfuse). Emitter is Logfire's OTel lib but Logfire SaaS is OPTIONAL (point
OTEL endpoint at Langfuse, send_to_logfire=false). CAVEAT (bounded): token/cost attribute mapping is the soft
spot (#2262/#4364 open) — affects cost analytics, NOT span structure. So dropping LangChain keeps Langfuse.

PYDANTIC AI MCP+FS+custom tools — CONFIRMED (docs): MCP via MCPServerStdio / MCPServerStreamableHTTP /
MCPServerSSE; custom tools via @agent.tool / @agent.tool_plain / tools=. FS = custom Python tools (reuse
rebar's fs_tools). Custom-tool use already validated LIVE on Anthropic in the runtime POC.

VISUAL POC (visual_bpmn_roundtrip_poc.mjs, bpmn-moddle ~15KB/3 deps/MIT — the HEADLESS layer, NOT the
browser editor): T1 PASS — with a registered `rebar` moddle descriptor, read/write/read preserves agent-step
metadata (prompt/provider/tools), all 11 stable ids, and multiInstance(fan-out). T2 (no descriptor) — unknown
extension is LAX-PRESERVED by bpmn-moddle (more robust than the forums implied); typed/guaranteed handling +
safety across bpmn-js editor save/copy cycles still wants the descriptor. T3 PASS — a simulated human edit
(rename + add a step) round-trips with the agent extension intact. => the IR<->BPMN serializer is FEASIBLE
and BOUNDED (~one moddle descriptor + round-trip fixtures).

DRAW.IO vs BPMN-JS (Joe's free-form concern) — VALIDATED + DECISIVE for bpmn-js. draw.io is free-form, no
domain metamodel, no validation ("you can't validate a drawing"; drawio->BPMN converters discard
non-conforming elements) -> arbitrary edits that don't map back = confusing/lossy UX (Joe's exact concern).
bpmn-js constrains editing to the BPMN metamodel (BpmnRules/canConnect; palette restricted; backed by
bpmn-moddle so it validates during modeling) -> edits can't drift outside the IR's vocabulary IF our IR maps
onto BPMN. => choose bpmn-js (constrained metamodel), NOT draw.io.

NOTE: bpmn-js (the EDITOR) is browser-bound (~50KB-hundreds-KB) + custom bpmn.io license (watermark); but the
EDITOR is an out-of-process edit-time tool, and the SERIALIZER only needs bpmn-moddle (MIT, light). DI/layout
must be generated (bpmn-auto-layout, all-or-nothing) — but since the visual format is EPHEMERAL we just
auto-layout on open; nothing persisted.

ALL 3 DE-RISK POCs now PASS: engine replay-correctness; runtime cross-provider+thinking-mitigation; visual
IR<->BPMN round-trip.

STRUCTURED-OUTPUT RELIABILITY (Joe: how do popular Pydantic projects guarantee schema-conforming output;
retire the second-interpreter LLM). RESEARCH VERDICT: the second-interpreter LLM IS a recognized anti-pattern
(can't validate non-determinism with more non-determinism). Converged LAYERED stack:
1. Provider-native CONSTRAINED decoding / strict json_schema where supported — OpenAI strict ~100% vs <40%
   unconstrained; Gemini responseSchema; **Anthropic native structured outputs now GA (constrained, compiled
   grammar; output_config.format + strict tools)** — via Pydantic AI NativeOutput; else PromptedOutput cross-

   constraining IMPROVED accuracy +4%, contra "Let Me Speak Freely" which itself used a 2nd-LLM parser a regex beat.)
2. Deterministic TOLERANT parse of near-miss output: json-repair (~5k*, pure Python) — no LLM, no retry. (BAML
   schema-aligned-parsing is the richer version but is a separate .baml DSL.)
3. Pydantic validation + normalizing validators — put numeric/length bounds HERE, not in the JSON Schema, to
   stay inside Anthropic's strict-grammar SUBSET (no recursion, no numeric/length bounds, <=20 strict tools).

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
PASS-1 review — criterion T5c (Security, overlay).

APPLICABILITY: T5c applies here only narrowly. This is a config-toggle + documentation follow-on (disable-the-gate config; a written rollback/back-out runbook; deploy-ordering for the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar + signature events). It adds NO new endpoint, network exposure, authn/authz boundary, or new credential. The one real security surface it TOUCHES is the existing HMAC signing scheme's secret lifecycle — and the underlying implementation is already sound (verified against src/rebar/signing.py): the key is never exposed (only a domain-separated SHA-256 fingerprint `key_id` is stored, signing.py:151-157), it resolves from `REBAR_SIGNING_KEY` or a gitignored, atomically-created 0o600 `<tracker>/.signing-key` file (signing.py:79-148), an empty/forgeable key fails loudly on sign and certifies nothing on verify (signing.py:107-118), and no key value is logged. So most of the T5c checklist PASSES not-applicable / already-sound.

AFFIRMATIONS (T5c):
- Secret lifecycle (checklist item 4) — the signing-key custody the plan's "signature scheme" rests on is already sound: env-var or 0o600 gitignored file, fingerprint-only exposure, never-log-the-secret, fail-loud on empty key. No plaintext-secret-in-code/IaC/logs surface is introduced by this plan.
- Access boundary (checklist item 1) — no new endpoint/path; the claim-path gate is an existing, opt-in, default-OFF preference (config.py:260) reusing the existing atomic claim primitive. No new authn/authz surface.
- Least-privilege (checklist item 3) — no new credential/role/grant introduced; nothing to scope.
- ANTI-FP honored: the verdict/fingerprint data the REVIEW_RESULT sidecar persists already lives in the repo/event log and is non-sensitive (per-criterion verdicts + content fingerprints), so its preserved-and-ignored rollout leaks nothing.

FINDING (one, coaching/non-blocking):

- [ ] Have the AC2 rollback/back-out runbook for the SIGNATURE SCHEME state the signing-key custody during rollout AND back-out — specifically that the runbook examples are fingerprint/placeholder-only (never echo or log a raw key or a real `REBAR_SIGNING_KEY`), and whether a rollout/back-out of the signing scheme involves the key at all (it should NOT require key rotation/exposure, since rollback is "turn the preference off" + the key never leaves the environment). As written, AC2 ("a written rollback/back-out plan ... for the signature scheme") under-specifies the secret-lifecycle posture of the rollout procedure it documents, which is the one genuinely security-relevant gap in this plan's domain.
  - criteria: T5c
  - location: Scope bullet 2 ("a documented rollback / back-out path for enabling the gate (and for the signature scheme)") + Acceptance Criteria line 2
  - evidence:
    - The plan's deliverable is a rollout/back-out RUNBOOK for "the signature scheme," and rollout runbooks for HMAC schemes are exactly where plaintext-key handling tends to leak in (example commands that `export REBAR_SIGNING_KEY=...` or echo the key). The plan never states the secret-lifecycle constraint the runbook must hold.
    - The existing source already enforces the right invariant the runbook must not undermine: key never exposed (signing.py:151-157, only `key_id` fingerprint persisted); injected via `REBAR_SIGNING_KEY` out-of-band or a gitignored 0o600 file (signing.py:14-18, 79-118). The runbook should explicitly preserve this (placeholder-only examples; no key rotation needed for a behavioral rollback).
  - suggested_fix: Add a one-line constraint to AC2/Scope bullet 2: "the signature-scheme rollback/rollout runbook uses placeholder/fingerprint-only key references (never a raw key or real REBAR_SIGNING_KEY in examples or logs), and a behavioral rollback (preference off) requires no key rotation or key exposure."
